human genetic susceptibility factors to TB are likely to be highly variable among different human populations.

the genetic basis of TB pathogenesis and aims at identifying genetic factors that are involved in the pathogenetic process of TB.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interplay between human and Mtb genomic variability is not yet sufficiently studied to draw a final conclusion on its importance for the pathogenesis of TB.
the interaction between Mtb and human genomic variability is a promising research field for TB research.
the interaction between host and pathogen genetic variation is an important factor to consider for future TB research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the genetic study of TB has been hampered by the lack of a systematic consideration of the genetic variability of the causative pathogen, and this has been particularly detrimental to the identification of major host susceptibility genes.
TB is a multifactorial disease, and that the genetic susceptibility to this infection and the development of disease is influenced by both the host and the pathogen.
the genetic study of TB is still in its early days, and the field is in urgent need of new ideas to overcome the challenges of the complex nature of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
human and mycobacterial genomic variability are not independent and should be jointly analyzed to better understand the complex interaction between host and pathogen in tuberculosis.
the genetic architecture of TB is complex, and that the interplay of host and pathogen genetic diversity may be crucial in understanding TB pathogenesis.
human–Mtb coevolution is a reality that should be taken into consideration when studying the genetic basis of TB.
